key_insight: An active particle suspension inside an elastic vesicle can self-organize the membrane into a sequence of distinct morphodynamic states, from stable vortical order to spinning, fluctuating, and turbulent shapes as activity increases.
engineering_relevance: The work shows how soft boundary design and anchoring interactions can be used to control, diagnose, or harness active flows in deformable microcapsules and bioinspired soft devices.
method: 2D weakly extensible elastic-ring model with bending rigidity
Kinetic-theory description of confined dilute extensile active particles
Hydrodynamic and energetic coupling solved with stability analysis plus immersed-boundary nonlinear simulations
evidence_signal: The abstract reports analytical stability thresholds and nonlinear simulation results that identify a hierarchy of shape instabilities and resulting emergent states.
watch_item: The model is two-dimensional and idealized, so quantitative transfer to real 3D vesicles may require care in calibration of anchoring strength, extensibility, and active-particle parameters.
paper_title: Active Sculpting: morphodynamics of internally stirred active vesicles
